question.problem:
Compute $P\left(  X \leq 3 \right)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14097680/assets/b083c72bc5c3bb6ea1a4f5036a57e5671c884d585def9e71f17a1ac72845d984.svg)
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a \leq X \leq  b) = \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x \lt  2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{2x}{45}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{45}\,{x}^{2}]}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{45}({3}^{2}-{2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{45}\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
